name: eia861-reliability-deterioration
description: Given three years of published distribution-reliability history and utility attributes, will a U.S. electric distribution utility's day-to-day outage duration (SAIDI excluding major event days) jump by at least 50% above its own recent norm in the next calendar year?
split_description: Cohorts are forecast years Y = 2016, 2017, ..., 2024 (labels in CY 2017 ... 2025). Fixed chronological boundaries: train = Y 2016-2019, eval = Y 2020-2021, holdout = Y 2022-2024. No random reassignment and no re-splitting after measurement. Purge rule enforced in code: every feature year is <= Y-1, so the newest training feature year is 2018 while the earliest scored label year is 2021; therefore no training row's feature vector contains a year used to compute any eval or holdout label. Rows whose four-year window (Y-3 ... Y+1) spans a utility-number change or a change of reporting standard are dropped rather than carried across splits.
